rationale: The user concern is continuous drift between an onboarded install and current platform expectations, not only a discrete package version event.
Every reconciliation area needs a baseline. Without a snapshot, reconcile check would be another doctor sweep with different branding.

decision: Keep security posture audit in doctor, not reconcile.
rationale: Security checks describe current safety properties. Reconciliation compares current expectations to a prior local anchor. Mixing them would create a kitchen-sink command.

decision: Default dashboard path is static build/open, not long-running serve.
rationale: A local HTTP server adds port/process lifecycle and localhost exposure. Static artifacts match the existing install-report posture and can later grow into serve mode if demand appears.

decision: Ship R0 and R1 in one executable child plan.
rationale: Capability drift is the first useful consumer of the install snapshot and is directly layered on the completed capability roadmap. R2-R4 remain future trigger-gated milestones.
